summary: Reviewed the tests in ReviewRoundCapTest.java (10 tests) and ReviewRoundCapArgumentValidityTest.java (6 tests) against scripts/check-reviewed.sh and scripts/review_rounds.py, in an isolated git worktree carrying the exact staged bytes (hash independently confirmed to match). Ran the full suite unmutated (16/16 green, both files compile) and applied 11 distinct hand-mutations to the two production scripts: f[1]==k -> substring match (kills exactly aROUNDSKeyThatAppearsMIDLINE..., nothing else -- matches the round-13 major precisely); the reason-requirement drop; a 'finish' inserted right after the argued-cap warn (defeats the majors-still-block property); the dropped baselines/review.txt pathspec (T1, now caught in the split-off file by anArgumentInADIFFERENTSTAGEDFileDoesNOTLiftTheCap and aFILENAMEThatMerelyMATCHESTheGuardAsAPattern); the no-task guard replaced with 'if false' (T2, now caught by verdictsThatNameNOTASKRefuseRatherThanCountingAsROUNDZERO); a BRE-style unescaped-dot task match; the ROUNDS>2 boundary moved to >3 (7 of 16 tests fail, so the boundary is tightly pinned, not just approximately); the disagreement-resolves-by-first-glob-hit regression; and git diff --cached replaced with git diff (worktree instead of index -- 3 tests fail). Every one of these was caught. One mutation survives all 16 tests: widening the awk added-line selector from /^\+/ to /^[-+]/, so a staged DELETION of a rounds: line also argues the cap. This is not a hidden gap -- it is T8/M4.31's third arm, explicitly named in backlog.md's M4.31 row (still 'todo') and cross-referenced in the ArgumentValidityTest javadoc itself, and I independently rediscovered it before reading that row. The digit-guard removal (T5) also still survives 16/16 and is likewise disclosed as a minor, defense-in-depth gap. Independently verified the M0.56 red-record-preservation claim: used tdd_scan.py's key-parts subcommand (not git history) to show the DECL+REMAINDER binding key for every one of the 10 kept tests is byte-identical whether the 6 moved tests exist in a reconstructed combined file or in the separate one, and confirmed via check-tdd.sh against the real staged tree that all 16 tests show 'observed failing first, unchanged since'. Diffed the two files' shared helper block (run/gate/Gate/scratch/verdict/out) byte-for-byte -- no divergence. Confirmed R1's prior false claim about ReviewRoundCapTest.java:29 ('the three that called themselves first, second, third') is gone from the current text, replaced with the corrected 'only two of the nine carry an ordinal'. T4 (javadoc claims both-roles-present AND no-unresolved-majors are both enforced by this suite, but only the majors half is pinned) remains open -- the both-roles-present check ('for ROLE in $REQUIRED_ROLES') is pre-existing, unmodified context in this diff, not new behaviour this task introduced, so leaving it untested here is defensible, though the class javadoc's phrasing is broader than what it actually constrains. Also independently reproduced the M4.34 packet-truncation bug while building this review (./scripts/review.sh context cut off partway through the diff at ~35KB) -- already filed and 'todo', not a new finding, but noted because it means the packet cannot be relied on for the full diff and I read the staged files directly instead, per the packet's own warning.

findings.summary: The class javadoc claims the design property is 'both-roles-present AND no-unresolved-majors STAY ENFORCED' under an argued cap, but only the no-unresolved-majors half is pinned by this suite (anARGUEDCapStillBLOCKSAnUnresolvedMajor). No fixture in either file ever omits one role's verdict file, so 'iterate only the first role in $REQUIRED_ROLES' survives 16/16. This is T4 from an earlier round, correctly left as a minor: the both-roles-present check is pre-existing context this diff does not modify, not new behaviour it introduces.
findings.failure_scenario: A later edit to check-reviewed.sh changes `for ROLE in $REQUIRED_ROLES; do` to check only the first required role. All 16 ReviewRoundCapTest*/ArgumentValidityTest tests stay green because every fixture writes both role files identically. The regression (a commit landing with only one role's verdict present) is invisible to this suite and would need ReviewRolesTest.java or a dedicated fixture to catch.

findings.summary: T5 from an earlier round remains open and reproduced independently: deleting the `case "$ROUNDS" in ''|*[!0-9]*)` digits guard leaves all 16 tests green. Correctly disclosed as defense-in-depth for an environmental failure mode (stray interpreter stderr) rather than an adversarial input, so leaving it untested is reasonable, but it is still an unconstrained line.
findings.failure_scenario: A future refactor of the ERRS/ROUNDS plumbing drops the digits guard. Under a normal run nothing changes. Under the specific fault this guard exists for (review_rounds.py emitting stray text on stdout with exit 0), ROUNDS becomes non-numeric, the `-gt 2` comparison fails with '[: integer expected', the cap block is skipped, and the gate exits 0 past round 2. No test in this suite exercises that path.

notes: No blocking or major finding. The one mutation that survives all 16 tests (added-vs-removed line, T8) is the same one I found independently before reading the prior artifact for it, and is already disclosed as M4.31's third arm in backlog.md ('todo'), cross-referenced from ArgumentValidityTest's own javadoc -- not raised again here. Hash verified against git diff --cached | sha256sum before this verdict was written; matches the packet and the task instructions exactly (78d13e9c27e5...).
